results.name: Martingale structure of the renewal model for the standard Collatz map
results.summary: In the renewal model of the standard Collatz map, where every tripling is followed by a halving, the iterates are not a martingale, but they become one once each coming tripling is booked in advance.
results.statement: Let $(B_n)_{n\ge0}$ be the Markov chain on $\{0,1\}$ with $\mathbb{P}(B_{n+1}=0\mid B_n=1)=1$ and $\mathbb{P}(B_{n+1}=0\mid B_n=0)=\mathbb{P}(B_{n+1}=1\mid B_n=0)=\tfrac12$, let $x_0>0$, and put $x_{n+1}=3x_n$ if $B_n=1$ and $x_{n+1}=x_n/2$ if $B_n=0$, with $\mathcal{F}_n=\sigma(B_0,\ldots,B_n)$ (the renewal model for the standard Collatz map, which sends an even $m$ to $m/2$ and an odd $m$ to $3m+1$, where $B_n$ models the parity of the $n$th iterate). Write $\delta^{*}=\log(\sqrt3/2)$. Then (i) the stationary law of the chain satisfies $\mathbb{P}(B_n=1)=\tfrac13$, and the fraction of odd steps (indices $i$ with $B_i=1$) among the first $n$ steps converges to $\tfrac13$ almost surely from any initial state; (ii) $(x_n)$ is not a martingale, since $\mathbb{E}[x_{n+1}\mid\mathcal{F}_n]=3x_n$ on $\{B_n=1\}$, but $M_n=3^{B_n}x_n$ is a martingale; (iii) $(\log x_n)$ is not a supermartingale, since its increment is $+\log3$ on $\{B_n=1\}$, but $\log M_n$ is a supermartingale with conditional drift $0$ on $\{B_n=1\}$ and $\delta^{*}$ on $\{B_n=0\}$; (iv) almost surely $\frac1n\log x_n\to\tfrac13\log3 - \tfrac23\log2=\tfrac13\log\tfrac34=\tfrac23\delta^{*}\approx -0.0959$; (v) if $\tau_1<\tau_2<\cdots$ are the successive times at which $B_n=1$, then $X_j=x_{\tau_j}$ satisfies $X_{j+1}=3X_j2^{-K_{j+1}}$, where $K_{j+1}=\tau_{j+1} - \tau_j - 1$ are independent with the Geometric$(\tfrac12)$ law $\mathbb{P}(K=k)=2^{-k}$ for $k\ge1$, and $(X_j)$ is a martingale because $\mathbb{E}[3\cdot2^{-K}]=3\sum_{k\ge1}4^{-k}=1$.
results.label: prop:ch3:standard

results.name: Exact parity autocorrelation function of the renewal model for the standard Collatz map
results.summary: In the renewal model of the standard Collatz map one step in three is odd and the parity autocorrelation at lag h is minus one half raised to the power h.
results.statement: Let $(B_n)_{n\ge0}$ be the Markov chain on $\{0,1\}$ with $\mathbb{P}(B_{n+1}=0\mid B_n=1)=1$ and $\mathbb{P}(B_{n+1}=0\mid B_n=0)=\mathbb{P}(B_{n+1}=1\mid B_n=0)=\tfrac12$ (the renewal model for the standard Collatz map, where $B_n$ models the parity of the $n$th iterate), started from its stationary law. Then $(B_n)$ is stationary with $\mathbb{P}(B_n=1)=\frac{1}{1+\mathbb{E}[K]}=\frac13$ and $\operatorname{Var}(B_n)=\frac29$, where $K$, the number of zeros between successive ones of the chain, has the Geometric$(\tfrac12)$ law $\mathbb{P}(K=k)=2^{-k}$ for $k\ge1$ (so $\mathbb{E}[K]=2$), and its autocorrelation function is $\rho(h)=\operatorname{Corr}(B_n,B_{n+h})=\bigl(-\tfrac12\bigr)^{h}$ for $h\ge0$.
results.label: thm:autocorr

results.name: Long run variance of the log path in the renewal model for the standard Collatz map
results.summary: The negative parity correlations of the renewal model cut the long run variance of the log path to one third of its value for independent parities with the same frequency, one in three, of odd steps.
results.statement: Let $(B_n)_{n\ge0}$ be the Markov chain on $\{0,1\}$ with $\mathbb{P}(B_{n+1}=0\mid B_n=1)=1$ and $\mathbb{P}(B_{n+1}=0\mid B_n=0)=\mathbb{P}(B_{n+1}=1\mid B_n=0)=\tfrac12$, started from any initial state, let $x_0>0$, and put $x_{n+1}=3x_n$ if $B_n=1$ and $x_{n+1}=x_n/2$ if $B_n=0$ (the renewal model for the standard Collatz map). Let $\rho(h)=(-\tfrac12)^h$ be the autocorrelation function of $(B_n)$. The autocorrelation factor is $\mathcal{A}:=1+2\sum_{h\ge1}\rho(h)=1+2\cdot\frac{-1/2}{1+1/2}=\frac13$, and the variance of the log path satisfies $\frac{\operatorname{Var}(\log x_n)}{n}\longrightarrow\mathcal{A}\cdot\frac29(\log6)^2=\frac{2}{27}(\log6)^2\approx0.2378$ as $n\to\infty$.
results.label: cor:longrun

results.name: The stopped martingale of the Bernoulli model is not uniformly integrable
results.summary: The martingale of the Bernoulli model, stopped when the iterate first drops to 1 or below, is not uniformly integrable, because the unabsorbed paths keep expected value at least the starting value minus 1 while their probability tends to zero.
results.statement: Let $x_0>1$ and let $\xi_1,\xi_2,\ldots$ be independent random variables with $\mathbb{P}(\xi_i=\tfrac12)=\mathbb{P}(\xi_i=\tfrac32)=\tfrac12$, and put $x_n=x_0\xi_1\cdots\xi_n$ (the Bernoulli model for the accelerated Collatz map) and $\tau=\inf\{n\ge0:x_n\le1\}$. Then $\tau<\infty$ almost surely, the stopped process $(x_{n\wedge\tau})_{n\ge0}$ is a nonnegative martingale converging almost surely to $x_\tau\le1$, and it is not uniformly integrable. More precisely, for every $n$, $\mathbb{E}\bigl[x_n\mathbf{1}_{\{\tau>n\}}\bigr]\ge x_0 - 1$, while $\mathbb{P}(\tau>n)\to0$ as $n\to\infty$.
results.label: prop:uimartingale

results.name: Passage time of the stride model with overshoot
results.summary: In the random stride model of the Collatz map, the expected number of strides for log x to fall to zero or below is the starting log x plus the mean overshoot, which lies between log 2 and 2 log 2, divided by log(4/3), the size of the drift.
results.statement: Consider the stride model of the Collatz map. Let $K_1,K_2,\dots$ be independent random variables with $\mathbb{P}(K_j=k)=2^{-k}$ for $k\ge1$ (the Geometric$(\tfrac12)$ law), fix $x_0>1$, and put $x_j=x_{j-1}\cdot3\cdot2^{-K_j}$, so that $\log x_j=\log x_0+\Delta_1+\dots+\Delta_j$ with $\Delta_j=\log3-K_j\log2$. Let $\tau$ be the first $j$ with $\log x_j\le0$, and let $O=-\log x_\tau\ge0$ be the overshoot below $0$ at time $\tau$. Then $\log2\le\mathbb{E}[O]<2\log2$ and \[\frac{\log x_0+\log2}{|\log(3/4)|}\le\mathbb{E}_{x_0}[\tau]<\frac{\log x_0+2\log2}{|\log(3/4)|}.\]
results.label: prop:ch4:passage

results.name: Stride descent theorem for the Syracuse map
results.summary: One Syracuse stride lowers log x exactly when the halving exponent is at least 2 and raises it exactly when x is 3 mod 4, with sharp bounds on the size of the change.
results.statement: Let $S$ be the Syracuse map on the odd positive integers, $S(x)=(3x+1)/2^{k}$ with $k=v_2(3x+1)$, where $v_2(m)$ is the exponent of the largest power of $2$ dividing $m$. Let $x\ge3$ be odd and $k=v_2(3x+1)$. (i) $\log S(x)-\log x=\log(3+1/x)-k\log2$. (ii) If $k\ge2$, then $S(x)<x$, $\log S(x)-\log x\le\log\bigl(\tfrac34+\tfrac1{4x}\bigr)<0$, and $\log S(x)-\log x\le\log(7/9)$, with equality exactly at $x=9$. (iii) If $k=1$, which happens exactly when $x\equiv3\pmod4$, then $S(x)=(3x+1)/2>x$ and $\log\tfrac32<\log S(x)-\log x=\log\bigl(\tfrac32+\tfrac1{2x}\bigr)\le\log\tfrac53$, with equality on the right exactly at $x=3$.
results.label: thm:stride

results.name: No monotone strong Lyapunov function for a single Syracuse stride
results.summary: No strictly increasing function of x is a strict or strong Lyapunov function for the Syracuse map, because every integer congruent to 3 mod 4, half of all odd integers, ascends in one stride.
results.statement: Let $S$ be the Syracuse map on the odd positive integers, $S(x)=(3x+1)/2^{v_2(3x+1)}$, where $v_2(m)$ is the exponent of the largest power of $2$ dividing $m$. Let $W$ be a strictly increasing function from the odd positive integers to $(0,\infty)$, and let $\rho\le1$. Then $W(S(x))>\rho\,W(x)$ for every $x\equiv3\pmod4$. In particular no strictly increasing $W$ is a strict Lyapunov function for $(S,\{1\})$ (one with $W(S(x))<W(x)$ for every odd $x\ne1$) or a strong Lyapunov function for $(S,\{1\})$ (one with $W>0$ and $W(S(x))\le\rho W(x)$ for every odd $x\ne1$, for some constant $\rho<1$), and the set of odd integers on which $W(S(x))\le\rho W(x)$ fails contains the residue class $3\bmod4$, which has natural density $\tfrac12$ among the odd integers; for $\rho=1$ the set on which it fails is exactly this class.
results.label: thm:nolyapunov

results.name: Exact behaviour of two Syracuse strides
results.summary: Over two Syracuse strides an odd integer decreases exactly when the two halving exponents sum to at least 4, which holds for half of the odd integers, and the largest two stride ascent is log(17/7), attained only at 7.
results.statement: Let $S$ be the Syracuse map on the odd positive integers, $S(x)=(3x+1)/2^{v_2(3x+1)}$, where $v_2(m)$ is the exponent of the largest power of $2$ dividing $m$. For odd $x$ write $k_1=v_2(3x+1)$, $k_2=v_2(3S(x)+1)$ and $S^{(2)}(x)=S(S(x))$. Let $x\ge3$ be odd. (i) $S^{(2)}(x)<x$ if and only if $k_1+k_2\ge4$. (ii) The odd integers with a two stride descent, that is with $S^{(2)}(x)<x$, have natural density exactly $\tfrac12$ among the odd integers. (iii) $\max_{x\ge3\text{ odd}}\bigl(\log S^{(2)}(x)-\log x\bigr)=\log\tfrac{17}{7}\approx0.8873$, attained only at $x=7$, where $S(7)=11$ and $S^{(2)}(7)=17$.
results.label: prop:ch4:twostride

results.name: No fixed horizon monotone certificate for Collatz descent
results.summary: For every fixed number J of strides, no strictly increasing function of x certifies descent over J Syracuse strides, because the odd integers congruent to minus 1 modulo 2 to the J+1 ascend for J strides in a row.
results.statement: Let $S$ be the Syracuse map on the odd positive integers, $S(x)=(3x+1)/2^{v_2(3x+1)}$, where $v_2(m)$ is the exponent of the largest power of $2$ dividing $m$, and let $S^{(J)}$ be its $J$th iterate. Fix $J\ge1$, $\rho\le1$ and a strictly increasing function $W$ from the odd positive integers to $(0,\infty)$. Then $W(S^{(J)}(x))>\rho\,W(x)$ for every odd $x\equiv-1\pmod{2^{J+1}}$, that is, for every $x=2^{J+1}q-1$ with $q\ge1$. This set is infinite and has natural density $2^{-J}$ among the odd integers. Moreover, along it, \[\frac{S^{(J)}(x)}{x}\longrightarrow\Bigl(\frac32\Bigr)^{J}\qquad(q\to\infty).\]
results.label: cor:ch4:multistride

results.name: The linear majorizer of log cannot certify Collatz descent
results.summary: In the stochastic model the tangent line majorizer of log x has a positive mean increment per step of the standard map while log x has a negative one, so the linear surrogate cannot certify descent.
results.statement: Let $T_0$ be the standard Collatz map, $T_0(x)=x/2$ for even $x$ and $T_0(x)=3x+1$ for odd $x$, and let $g(y\mid x)=\log x+(y-x)/x$ be the tangent line majorizer of $\log$ at $x$, so that the surrogate increment $g(T_0(x)\mid x)-g(x\mid x)$ equals $-\tfrac12$ for even $x$ and $2+1/x$ for odd $x$. Under the stochastic model for the standard map, in which the parities of successive steps form a stationary renewal chain $(B_n)$ on $\{0,1\}$ (with $B_n=1$ for an odd step; an odd step is always followed by an even step, and an even step is followed by an odd or an even step with probability $\tfrac12$ each), so that a step is odd with stationary probability $\tfrac13$, the mean surrogate increment per step of $T_0$ is $\tfrac13\cdot2+\tfrac23\cdot\bigl(-\tfrac12\bigr)=+\tfrac13>0$, up to the $O(1/x)$ term, whereas the mean true increment per step is $\tfrac13\log3-\tfrac23\log2=\tfrac13\log(3/4)\approx-0.0959<0$. Per Syracuse stride, that is one odd step followed by $k$ even steps, in the stride model with $k$ distributed as Geometric$(\tfrac12)$ on $\{1,2,\dots\}$, the per step surrogate increments summed over the stride, with the majorizer recentred at every step, have mean $+1$ up to the $O(1/x)$ term, and the mean true increment is $\log(3/4)\approx-0.2877$.
results.label: prop:mmfails

results.name: Power majorizers of log and the Wald root of the stride model
results.summary: In the stride model the power majorizers of log with exponent strictly between 0 and 1 have strictly negative mean increment, interpolating between the true drift log(3/4) and the zero drift of the linear majorizer at the Wald root 1.
results.statement: Work in the stride model of the Collatz map, in which the log increment of one stride is $\Delta=\log3-K\log2$ with $K$ distributed as Geometric$(\tfrac12)$ on $\{1,2,\dots\}$, and write $M(p)=\mathbb{E}[e^{p\Delta}]=3^{p}/(2^{1+p}-1)$. For $0<p\le1$ let $g_p(y\mid x)=\log x+\frac{(y/x)^{p}-1}{p}$; each $g_p$ dominates $\log y$ and is tangent to it at $y=x$, and $p=1$ is the tangent line (linear) majorizer of $\log$. Then the mean stride increment of the surrogate $g_p$, ignoring the $1/x$ correction, is $(M(p)-1)/p$, and: (i) $M(0)=M(1)=1$, and $M(p)<1$ for $0<p<1$; (ii) $p\mapsto(M(p)-1)/p$ is increasing on $(0,1]$, tends to $\mathbb{E}[\Delta]=\log(3/4)$ as $p\downarrow0$, and equals $0$ at $p=1$. In particular every power majorizer with $0<p<1$ has strictly negative mean surrogate increment, and the linear majorizer $p=1$ sits exactly on the boundary.
results.label: prop:ch4:power

results.name: No residue potential for the Collatz map at any modulus
results.summary: No potential made of log x plus a function of residues modulo a power of 2 decreases at every step of the accelerated Collatz map for all large x, because the residue graph has cycles of positive weight, such as the loop at minus 1.
results.statement: Let $T$ be the accelerated Collatz map, $T(x)=x/2$ for even $x$ and $T(x)=(3x+1)/2$ for odd $x$. Fix $d\ge1$ and let $G_d$ be the directed graph on the residues modulo $2^d$ in which the residue $a$ has an edge to each residue $a'$ with $a'\equiv T(a)\pmod{2^{d-1}}$ (the two lifts of $T(a)$), with weight $w(a)=\log(3/2)$ if $a$ is odd and $w(a)=-\log2$ if $a$ is even. (i) There are a function $\varphi$ on $\mathbb{Z}/2^d\mathbb{Z}$ and a bound $X$ such that $V(T(x))<V(x)$ for all integers $x\ge X$, where $V(x)=\log x+\varphi(x\bmod2^d)$, if and only if every cycle of $G_d$ has negative total weight. (ii) For every $d\ge1$ the graph $G_d$ contains cycles of positive weight: the loop at $-1$, of weight $\log(3/2)$, and the images of the cycles of $T$ on the negative integers, whose weights are $r\log3-s\log2>0$ for a cycle with $r$ odd steps among $s$ steps. The maximum cycle mean of $G_d$ is exactly $\log(3/2)$ for every $d$. (iii) Consequently no potential $\log x+\varphi(x\bmod2^d)$ with bounded $\varphi$ decreases at every step for all large $x$, for any $d$, and the same holds for potentials required to decrease over any fixed number $J$ of steps.
results.label: thm:ch5c:residue

results.name: Surplus of a pointwise potential along runs of trailing ones
results.summary: A potential log x plus a correction that decreases at every Syracuse stride needs an unbounded correction, with a surplus growing linearly in the number of trailing ones of x.
results.statement: Let $S$ be the Syracuse map on the odd positive integers, $S(x)=(3x+1)/2^{v_2(3x+1)}$, where $v_2(m)$ is the exponent of the largest power of $2$ dividing $m$, and let $V(x)=\log x+\varphi(x)$ for a real function $\varphi$ on the odd positive integers. Suppose $V(S(x))<V(x)$ for every odd $x\ge3$. Then for every $j\ge2$ and every odd $q\ge1$, \[\varphi(2^jq-1)-\varphi(2\cdot3^{j-1}q-1)\;>\;(j-1)\log\frac32 .\] In particular $\varphi$ is unbounded above or below, and $\sup\varphi-\inf\varphi\ge(j-1)\log(3/2)$ for every $j$.
results.label: prop:ch5c:surplus

results.name: Run length potential and its failure fraction
results.summary: With weight c above log(3/2), the run length potential log x plus c times the 2 adic valuation of x+1 decreases at all but finitely many ascending strides, but under the stride model it fails to decrease at a positive fraction of odd integers, 0.2087 at weight c equal to 1.
results.statement: Let $S$ be the Syracuse map on the odd positive integers, $S(x)=(3x+1)/2^{k}$ with $k=v_2(3x+1)$, where $v_2(m)$ is the exponent of the largest power of $2$ dividing $m$, let $\varepsilon(x)=\log\bigl(1+\tfrac1{3x}\bigr)$, and for $c>\log(3/2)$ let $V_c(x)=\log x+c\,v_2(x+1)$. Then $V_c$ decreases at every ascending stride (a stride with $k=1$) from an odd $x>1/\bigl(2(e^c-3/2)\bigr)$, hence at every ascending stride when $c>\log(5/3)$ and at all but finitely many when $c\le\log(5/3)$. The descending strides ($k\ge2$) at which $V_c$ fails to decrease are exactly those $x\mapsto y=S(x)$, with $k$ halvings, that land on a $y$ with $v_2(y+1)-1\ge(k\log2-\log3-\varepsilon(x))/c$. Under the stride model, in which $k$ and $v_2(y+1)$ are independent Geometric$(\tfrac12)$ variables on $\{1,2,\dots\}$, the fraction of odd $x$ at which $V_c$ fails to decrease is \[p(c)=\sum_{k\ge2}2^{-k}\,2^{-\lceil(k\log2-\log3)/c\rceil},\] which is $0.2087$ at $c=1$ and decreases to $0.1431$ as $c\downarrow\log(3/2)$, and $V_c$ fails at a positive fraction of odd integers for every $c$.
results.label: prop:ch5c:runpot

results.name: The extrapolated point of Switching MM is a long gradient step
results.summary: For every differentiable objective, two consecutive steps of Switching MM from an even index are exactly a long gradient step, longer by the factor one plus the momentum coefficient, followed by a plain gradient step.

Let $f:\mathbb{R}^d	o\mathbb{R}$ be differentiable, let $\alpha>0$, and write $G_h(x)=x-h

results.name: Two step equivalence of Switching MM with cyclic gradient steps on quadratics
results.summary: On a strongly convex quadratic, two steps of Switching MM from an even index equal a plain gradient step followed by a longer one, so the method is a cyclic step size method and every two steps its error is multiplied by an explicit degree two polynomial of the Hessian.
results.statement:
Let $f(x)=	frac12x^	op Ax-b^	op x$ with $A$ symmetric positive definite and minimizer $x^\ast=A^{-1}b$, let $\alpha>0$ and $ eta\ge0$, write $G_h(x)=x-h
abla f(x)$, and let $(x_t)$ be generated by Switching MM with step $\alpha$ and momentum coefficient $ eta$ (it starts from $x_{-1}=x_0$, takes the plain gradient step $x_{t+1}=x_t-\alpha

For every even $t\ge0$, $x_{t+2}=G_{(1+ eta)\alpha}(x_{t+1})=G_{(1+ eta)\alpha} igl(G_\alpha(x_t) igr)$, that is, two steps of Switching MM from an even index are a gradient step of length $\alpha$ followed by a gradient step of length $(1+ eta)\alpha$, and every iterate of Switching MM is an iterate of this cyclic schedule. In terms of the error $e_t=x_t-x^\ast$, $e_{t+2}=(I-\alpha A) igl(I-(1+ eta)\alpha A igr)e_t$ for even $t$.
results.label: thm:smmquad

results.name: Stability range and linear convergence of Switching MM on quadratics
results.summary: Switching MM converges linearly on every strongly convex quadratic for any momentum coefficient below one and step at most one over L, and it is stable exactly for normalized steps below an explicit limit.
results.statement: Let $f(x)=\tfrac12x^\top Ax-b^\top x$ with $A$ symmetric positive definite whose largest eigenvalue is $L$, let $\alpha>0$ and $0\le\beta<1$, and let Switching MM with step $\alpha$ and momentum coefficient $\beta$ (it starts from $x_{-1}=x_0$, takes the plain gradient step $x_{t+1}=x_t-\alpha\nabla f(x_t)$ at even $t$, and at odd $t$ takes the extrapolated step $x_{t+1}=y_t-\alpha\nabla f(y_t)$ with $y_t=x_t+\beta(x_t-x_{t-1})$) have the two step multiplier $\rho(a)=(1-a)\bigl(1-(1+\beta)a\bigr)=1-(2+\beta)a+(1+\beta)a^2$ on an eigendirection with eigenvalue $\lambda$ and normalized step $a=\alpha\lambda$. Then for real $a$, $|\rho(a)|<1$ if and only if $0<a<(2+\beta)/(1+\beta)$. In particular Switching MM converges linearly on every strongly convex quadratic whenever $\alpha\le1/L$, and in fact whenever $\alpha L<(2+\beta)/(1+\beta)$. For all $a>0$, $\rho(a)\ge1-(2+\beta)^2/\bigl(4(1+\beta)\bigr)$, a minimum attained at $a=(2+\beta)/\bigl(2(1+\beta)\bigr)$.
results.label: cor:ch6:stability

results.name: Slow mode effective step of Switching MM on quadratics
results.summary: In the slow directions Switching MM behaves like gradient descent with a step enlarged by the factor two plus beta over two, about 1.29 at the Collatz momentum, so it is not an accelerated method.
results.statement: Let $f(x)=\tfrac12x^\top Ax-b^\top x$ with $A$ symmetric positive definite, let $\alpha>0$ and $\beta\ge0$, and let Switching MM with step $\alpha$ and momentum coefficient $\beta$ (it starts from $x_{-1}=x_0$, takes the plain gradient step $x_{t+1}=x_t-\alpha\nabla f(x_t)$ at even $t$, and at odd $t$ takes the extrapolated step $x_{t+1}=y_t-\alpha\nabla f(y_t)$ with $y_t=x_t+\beta(x_t-x_{t-1})$) have the two step multiplier $\rho(a)=(1-a)\bigl(1-(1+\beta)a\bigr)$ on an eigendirection with eigenvalue $\lambda$ and normalized step $a=\alpha\lambda$ (that is, the error component along that eigenvector satisfies $e_{t+2}=\rho(a)e_t$ for even $t$). As $a\to0$, $\rho(a)=1-(2+\beta)a+O(a^2)$, and the per step contraction factor $|\rho(a)|^{1/2}$ equals $1-\tfrac{2+\beta}{2}a+O(a^2)$. Thus in the slow directions Switching MM behaves like gradient descent with the effective step $m_{\mathrm{SMM}}\,\alpha$, where $m_{\mathrm{SMM}}=\tfrac{2+\beta}{2}$, which is $1.2925$ at $\beta=\log_23-1$.
results.label: cor:ch6:slow

results.summary: For objectives with a Lipschitz Hessian, the failure of the odd iterates of Switching MM to follow a cyclic gradient path is of third order in the step size, and it vanishes for quadratics.

results.name: Exact stationary variance of Switching MM under additive gradient noise
results.summary: An exact formula for the stationary variance of Switching MM on a quadratic with additive gradient noise, for even iterates, odd iterates and their phase average, as a rational function of the normalized step and the momentum coefficient.
results.statement: Let $f(x)=\tfrac12x^\top Ax-b^\top x$ with $A$ symmetric positive definite and minimizer $x^\ast$, and suppose the algorithm sees the noisy gradient $g(x)=\nabla f(x)+\xi$, where a fresh $\xi$ is drawn at every call, independent of the past, with mean zero and covariance $\sigma^2I$. Run Switching MM with step $\alpha>0$ and momentum coefficient $0\le\beta<1$ with $g$ in place of $\nabla f$ (it starts from $x_{-1}=x_0$, takes the plain step $x_{t+1}=x_t-\alpha g(x_t)$ at even $t$, and at odd $t$ takes the extrapolated step $x_{t+1}=y_t-\alpha g(y_t)$ with $y_t=x_t+\beta(x_t-x_{t-1})$). Fix an eigenvalue $\lambda$ of $A$ with normalized step $a=\alpha\lambda\in(0,1]$, let $e_t$ be the component of $x_t-x^\ast$ along its eigenvector and $\xi_t$ the component of the noise drawn at iteration $t$ (independent, mean zero, variance $\sigma^2$), and put $\rho=(1-a)\bigl(1-(1+\beta)a\bigr)$. (i) For every even $t$, $e_{t+2}=\rho\,e_t+w_t$ with $w_t=-(1-a)(1+\beta)\alpha\,\xi_t-\alpha\,\xi_{t+1}$, where the $w_t$ for even $t$ are independent, independent of $e_t$, with mean zero and $\operatorname{Var}(w_t)=\alpha^2\sigma^2\bigl[(1-a)^2(1+\beta)^2+1\bigr]$. (ii) As $t\to\infty$ through even values, $\operatorname{Var}(e_t)$ converges to $V_{\mathrm{even}}=\alpha^2\sigma^2\bigl[(1-a)^2(1+\beta)^2+1\bigr]/(1-\rho^2)$, and through odd values to $V_{\mathrm{odd}}=(1-a)^2V_{\mathrm{even}}+\alpha^2\sigma^2$. (iii) The phase averaged stationary variance $V_{\mathrm{SMM}}=\tfrac12(V_{\mathrm{even}}+V_{\mathrm{odd}})$ satisfies $V_{\mathrm{SMM}}(a)/(\alpha^2\sigma^2)=Q(a,\beta)/(1-\rho^2)$, where $Q(a,\beta)=(2+2\beta+\beta^2)-(1+\beta)(2+3\beta)\,a+(1+\beta)(1+3\beta)\,a^2-\beta(1+\beta)\,a^3$ and $1-\rho^2=a\bigl(2+\beta-(1+\beta)a\bigr)\bigl(2-(2+\beta)a+(1+\beta)a^2\bigr)$.
results.label: thm:smmvar

results.name: Slow mode noise amplification of Switching MM
results.summary: In the slow modes Switching MM amplifies gradient noise, relative to gradient descent at the same step, by an explicit function of the momentum coefficient that equals 1.359 at the Collatz value.
results.statement: Let $f(x)=\tfrac12x^\top Ax-b^\top x$ with $A$ symmetric positive definite, with the noisy gradient oracle $g(x)=\nabla f(x)+\xi$ (a fresh $\xi$ at every call, independent of the past, mean zero, covariance $\sigma^2I$), and run Switching MM with step $\alpha>0$ and momentum coefficient $0\le\beta<1$ with $g$ in place of $\nabla f$ (plain step at even $t$, extrapolated step $x_{t+1}=y_t-\alpha g(y_t)$ with $y_t=x_t+\beta(x_t-x_{t-1})$ at odd $t$). On the eigendirection of an eigenvalue $\lambda$ with normalized step $a=\alpha\lambda\in(0,1]$, let $V_{\mathrm{even}}$ and $V_{\mathrm{odd}}$ be the limits of the variance of the error component along even and odd times, $V_{\mathrm{SMM}}=\tfrac12(V_{\mathrm{even}}+V_{\mathrm{odd}})$, and $V_{\mathrm{GD}}(a)=\alpha^2\sigma^2/\bigl(a(2-a)\bigr)$ the stationary variance of noisy gradient descent $e_{t+1}=(1-a)e_t-\alpha\xi_t$ with the same step. As $a\to0$, both $aV_{\mathrm{even}}$ and $aV_{\mathrm{odd}}$ converge to $\alpha^2\sigma^2\,\dfrac{(1+\beta)^2+1}{2(2+\beta)}=\alpha^2\sigma^2\,\dfrac{1+\beta+\beta^2/2}{2+\beta}$. Consequently $\lim_{a\to0}V_{\mathrm{SMM}}(a)/V_{\mathrm{GD}}(a)=V(\beta):=\dfrac{2+2\beta+\beta^2}{2+\beta}=\beta+\dfrac{2}{2+\beta}$.
results.label: cor:ch7:slow

results.name: Noise bound for Switching MM uniform in the normalized step
results.summary: On a quadratic with additive gradient noise, on every eigendirection with normalized step up to one, the stationary variance of Switching MM lies between that of gradient descent and 5/3 times it, uniformly over momentum coefficients below one, whereas every step momentum amplifies slow mode noise by a factor that grows without bound as the coefficient tends to one.
results.statement: Let $f(x)=\tfrac12x^\top Ax-b^\top x$ with $A$ symmetric positive definite, with the noisy gradient oracle $g(x)=\nabla f(x)+\xi$ (a fresh $\xi$ at every call, independent of the past, mean zero, covariance $\sigma^2I$), and run Switching MM with step $\alpha>0$ and momentum coefficient $0\le\beta<1$ with $g$ in place of $\nabla f$. On the eigendirection of an eigenvalue $\lambda$ with normalized step $a=\alpha\lambda\in(0,1]$, let $V_{\mathrm{SMM}}(a)$ be the phase averaged stationary variance of the error component (the average of its limits along even and odd times), $V_{\mathrm{GD}}(a)=\alpha^2\sigma^2/\bigl(a(2-a)\bigr)$ the stationary variance of noisy gradient descent with the same step, and $V(\beta)=\beta+2/(2+\beta)$. Then for $0\le\beta<1$ and every $a\in(0,1]$, $V_{\mathrm{GD}}(a)\le V_{\mathrm{SMM}}(a)\le V(\beta)\,V_{\mathrm{GD}}(a)<\tfrac53\,V_{\mathrm{GD}}(a)$, with $V_{\mathrm{SMM}}(a)=V_{\mathrm{GD}}(a)$ only when $\beta=0$ or $a=1$, and $V_{\mathrm{SMM}}(a)=V(\beta)\,V_{\mathrm{GD}}(a)$ only when $\beta=0$.
results.label: prop:ch7:uniform

results.name: Noise floor at matched speed for momentum methods and Switching MM
results.summary: At matched slow mode speed Switching MM pays a small noise floor penalty over gradient descent, 1.051 at the Collatz momentum and at most 10/9; it is the period two analogue of the result of Yuan, Ying and Sayed (2016) that every step heavy ball and Nesterov match gradient descent exactly.
results.statement: Consider noisy gradient methods on a strongly convex quadratic with additive gradient noise of variance $\sigma^2$ and step $\alpha$, in the slow mode limit $a=\alpha\lambda\to0$ along an eigendirection. A method has the effective step multiplier $m$ if its slow mode contracts like gradient descent with step $m\alpha$ (and gradient descent with step $m\alpha$ has slow mode variance $m$ times that at step $\alpha$), and the slow mode variance amplification $V$ if its stationary variance is $V$ times that of gradient descent at step $\alpha$. Its noise floor at matched speed relative to gradient descent is $V/m$. For momentum coefficient $0\le\beta<1$, this equals $1$ for every step heavy ball and for every step Nesterov momentum (where $V=m=1/(1-\beta)$), and for Switching MM (where $m=(2+\beta)/2$ and $V=(2+2\beta+\beta^2)/(2+\beta)$) it equals $\dfrac{2(2+2\beta+\beta^2)}{(2+\beta)^2}=1+\dfrac{\beta^2}{(2+\beta)^2}\ge1$, which is $1.051$ at $\beta=\log_23-1$ and increases to $10/9$ as $\beta\to1$. More generally, for any period two cyclic gradient step schedule with steps $h_1\alpha$ and $h_2\alpha$ the ratio is $\tfrac12(h_1^2+h_2^2)\big/\bigl(\tfrac12(h_1+h_2)\bigr)^2\ge1$, with equality only for equal steps.
results.label: prop:ch7:matched

results.name: Gain weight theorem for the noise floor of periodic first order methods
results.summary: For any linear periodic first order method on a quadratic that is stable at zero normalized step and has positive total gain, the slow mode noise floor at matched speed relative to gradient descent is a Cauchy and Schwarz ratio of the step gains, at least one, and equal to one only when all gains are equal.
results.statement: Fix a period $p\ge1$ and a memory length $K\ge1$. On one eigendirection of a quadratic with normalized step $a=\alpha\lambda$, with the state $z_t=(e_t,\dots,e_{t-K+1})$ of past errors, a linear periodic first order method evaluates at step $t$, with residue $j=t\bmod p$, the gradient at the extrapolated point $y_t=\gamma_j\cdot z_t$ and updates $e_{t+1}=\delta_j\cdot z_t-h_j\bigl(a\,y_t+\alpha\xi_t\bigr)$, where $\gamma_j,\delta_j\in\mathbb{R}^K$ and the step multipliers $h_j>0$ are fixed, and the gradient noise $\xi_t$ has mean zero, is uncorrelated across steps and has variance $\sigma^2$. Consistency requires $\delta_j\cdot\iota=\gamma_j\cdot\iota=1$ for $\iota=(1,\dots,1)$. Let $S_j(a)$ be the step matrix mapping $z_t$ to $z_{t+1}$ without noise (its first row is $(\delta_j-a\,h_j\gamma_j)^\top$ and its other rows shift the entries of $z_t$ down by one place), and write the product of the $p$ step matrices of one period as $B(a)=B_0+aB_1+O(a^2)$. Assume the method is stable at $a=0$: the eigenvalue $1$ of $B_0$, with right eigenvector $\iota$, is simple and all other eigenvalues of $B_0$ lie strictly inside the unit disc. Let $w$ be the left eigenvector of $B_0$ for the eigenvalue $1$ with $w\cdot\iota=1$. The gain of the $i$th step of the period is $c_i=h_i\,w\cdot\Pi_iu_1$, where $u_1$ is the first unit vector and $\Pi_i$ is the product, at $a=0$, of the step matrices of steps $i+1,\dots,p$ of the period, and $M=\sum_{i=1}^pc_i$, which is assumed to be positive. Then, as $a\to0$: (i) the per step contraction of the slow mode is $1-(M/p)\,a+O(a^2)$; (ii) the phase averaged stationary variance of $e_t$ is $\alpha^2\sigma^2\,\dfrac{\sum_ic_i^2}{2Ma}\,(1+o(1))$; (iii) consequently the noise floor relative to gradient descent run at the same slow mode speed, with step $(M/p)\alpha$, is $\mathcal F=\dfrac{p\sum_{i=1}^pc_i^2}{\bigl(\sum_{i=1}^pc_i\bigr)^2}\ge1$, with equality if and only if all gains are equal.
results.label: thm:ch7:gainweight

results.name: Rate and noise Pareto frontier for period two step schedules
results.summary: For period two cyclic gradient steps, the worst case contraction and the noise floor at matched speed depend on the step ratio through one number, which gives the exact Pareto frontier between rate and noise, ending at the Chebyshev schedule.
results.statement: Let $f$ be a quadratic whose Hessian has its spectrum in $[\mu,L]$, with $\kappa=L/\mu$, and consider gradient descent with cyclic steps $h_1,h_2$ (alternating absolute step lengths) of ratio $r=h_2/h_1\ge1$, under additive gradient noise. Put $G(r)=\dfrac{(1+r)^2}{4r}\ge1$. The worst case two step contraction over $[\mu,L]$ is $\max_{\lambda\in[\mu,L]}|(1-h_1\lambda)(1-h_2\lambda)|$, and the slow mode noise floor at matched speed is the slow mode stationary variance divided by that of gradient descent with the constant step of the same slow mode speed. (i) The slow mode noise floor at matched speed is $N=\dfrac{2(h_1^2+h_2^2)}{(h_1+h_2)^2}=2-\dfrac1{G(r)}$. (ii) For fixed $r$ with $G(r)\le G_{\mathrm{ch}}(\kappa)=\dfrac{2(\kappa+1)^2}{\kappa^2+6\kappa+1}$, the smallest possible worst case two step contraction over $[\mu,L]$ is $R^\ast(r)=1-\dfrac{4\kappa\,G(r)}{(\kappa+1)^2}$, attained when the steps are scaled so that $h_1+h_2=4G(r)/(\mu+L)$. For $G(r)>G_{\mathrm{ch}}(\kappa)$ the smallest worst case contraction exceeds that of the Chebyshev ratio. (iii) Consequently the Pareto frontier between rate and noise floor is $R=1-\dfrac{4\kappa}{(2-N)(\kappa+1)^2}$ for $1\le N\le N_{\mathrm{ch}}(\kappa)$, where $N_{\mathrm{ch}}=\dfrac{3\kappa^2+2\kappa+3}{2(\kappa+1)^2}$ is the noise floor of the two step Chebyshev schedule (the period two schedule minimizing the worst case two step contraction over $[\mu,L]$), whose ratio tends to $(1+\sqrt2)^2=5.83$ and whose floor tends to $3/2$ as $\kappa\to\infty$.
results.label: prop:ch7:pareto

results.name: Switching MM under multiplicative gradient noise
results.summary: Under multiplicative gradient noise Switching MM has a closed form stationary second moment, an unchanged slow mode ratio to gradient descent under least squares scaling, and a mean square stability threshold given by the gains under diffusive scaling.
results.statement:
Consider on one eigendirection of a quadratic with eigenvalue $\lambda$ and normalized step $a=\alpha\lambda$ the oracle $g(y)=(\lambda+\eta_t)\,e_y+\xi_t$ for the gradient at a point with error $e_y$ along that eigenvector, where $\eta_t,\xi_t$ are independent of the past, with mean zero, uncorrelated with each other, $\operatorname{Var}(\alpha\eta_t)=\omega^2$ and $\operatorname{Var}(\xi_t)=\sigma^2$. For Switching MM with step $\alpha$ and momentum coefficient $0\le eta<1$ the second moments of the error obey a closed linear recursion: with $
u_1=(1-a)^2+\omega^2$ and $
u_2= igl(1-(1+ eta)a igr)^2+(1+ eta)^2\omega^2$, the stationary second moment at even times is $\alpha^2\sigma^2 igl(
u_1(1+ eta)^2+1 igr)/(1-
u_1
u_2)$, finite if and only if $
u_1
u_2<1$. As $a	o0$: (i) under the least squares scaling $\omega^2=\vartheta a^2$ with $\vartheta$ fixed (the relative curvature noise, $\vartheta=2$ for a Gaussian regressor), the slow mode ratio of the stationary second moment of Switching MM to that of gradient descent with the same step and noise is unchanged, equal to $(2+2 eta+ eta^2)/(2+ eta)$ for every $\vartheta$; (ii) under the diffusive scaling $\omega^2=\epsilon a$, for any linear periodic first order method of period $p$ on this eigendirection (with state $z_t=(e_t,\dots,e_{t-K+1})$ and residue $j=t mod p$ it sets $e_{t+1}=\delta_j\cdot z_t-h_j\alpha igl((\lambda+\eta_t)y_t+\xi_t igr)$ with $y_t=\gamma_j\cdot z_t$, where $\gamma_j,\delta_j\in\mathbb{R}^K$ with $\gamma_j\cdot\iota=\delta_j\cdot\iota=1$ for $\iota=(1,\dots,1)$ and $h_j>0$ are fixed) that is stable at $a=0$ (the product $B_0$ of its step matrices over one period at $a=0$ has the simple eigenvalue $1$ and all its other eigenvalues strictly inside the unit disc) and has $M>0$, where $c_i=h_i\,w\cdot\Pi_iu_1$ is the gain of step $i$ ($w$ the left eigenvector of $B_0$ for the eigenvalue $1$ with $w\cdot\iota=1$, $u_1$ the first unit vector, $\Pi_i$ the product at $a=0$ of the step matrices of steps $i+1,\dots,p$) and $M=\sum_ic_i$, the stationary second moment of the error satisfies $a\,\mathbb{E}[e^2]	o\alpha^2\sigma^2\sum_ic_i^2 ig/ igl(2M-\epsilon\sum_ic_i^2 igr)$, so that the method is mean square stable for small $a$ exactly when $\epsilon<\epsilon^\ast=2M/\sum_ic_i^2$.
results.label: prop:ch7:mult

results.name: Certified growth exponents for the inverse Collatz tree from a simplified difference inequality method
results.summary: A simplified version of the Krasikov difference inequality method turns lower bounds on how many integers reach a given number into a finite supersolution test over residues modulo a power of 3, and certifies exponents up to 0.477, far below the best known 0.84.
results.statement:
Let $T$ be the accelerated Collatz map, $T(n)=n/2$ for even $n$ and $T(n)=(3n+1)/2$ for odd $n$. For an integer $n
ot\equiv0\pmod 3$ and $X\ge1$ let $\pi_n(X)=\#\{m\le Xn:\ 	ext{the orbit of }m	ext{ under }T	ext{ passes through }n\}$. For an integer $j\ge1$ and $n
ot\equiv0\pmod3$ with $2^jn\equiv2\pmod3$ put $c_j(n)=(2^{j+1}n-1)/3$, the odd preimage of $2^jn$, and call $j$ fertile for $n$ if $2^jn\equiv2$ or $8\pmod9$. Fix $k\ge1$ and let $\mathcal R_k$ be the set of residues modulo $3^k$ prime to $3$. For $g>0$ and a positive vector $(w_r)_{r\in\mathcal R_k}$ define $(\Phi_gw)_r=\min_{\ell}\sum_{j\ \mathrm{fertile\ for}\ \ell} igl(3/2^{j+1} igr)^g\,w_{[c_j(\ell)]}$, where the minimum is over the three lifts $\ell$ of $r$ to residues modulo $3^{k+1}$, the sum is over all $j\ge1$, and fertility of $j$ and the class $[c_j(\ell)]\in\mathcal R_k$ (the residue of $c_j(n)$ modulo $3^k$ for any integer $n\equiv\ell$) depend only on $\ell$ and $j$. If $\Phi_gw\ge(1+\eta)w$ componentwise for some $\eta>0$, then there is $C>0$ such that $\pi_n(X)\ge C\,w_{[n]}\,X^g$ for all $X\ge1$ and all $n
ot\equiv0\pmod3$ not lying on a cycle of $T$, where $[n]$ is the residue of $n$ modulo $3^k$.
results.label: thm:ch5b:exponent

results.name: Counting bound with exponent 0.477 for integers reaching 1
results.summary: The simplified method certifies, with a vector found by computer and checked in exact integer arithmetic, that at least x to the power 0.477 integers up to x reach 1, below the exponent 0.84 of Krasikov and Lagarias (2003).
results.statement: For all sufficiently large $x$, at least $x^{0.477}$ integers $m\le x$ have orbits under the accelerated Collatz map $T$ ($T(n)=n/2$ for even $n$ and $T(n)=(3n+1)/2$ for odd $n$) that reach $1$.
results.label: cor:ch5b:count

results.name: Switching MM decreases the objective on alternate iterates for every smooth function
results.summary: Switching MM with step one over L decreases the objective on alternate iterates for every L smooth function, convex or not, with an explicit decrease that yields a bound on the smallest gradient norm.
results.statement:
Let $f:\mathbb{R}^d	o\mathbb{R}$ be $L$ smooth (its gradient is Lipschitz with constant $L$) and bounded below by $f_{\inf}$, and run Switching MM with step $1/L$ and momentum coefficient $ eta\in[0,1)$ (it starts from $x_{-1}=x_0$, takes the plain gradient step $x_{t+1}=x_t-
abla f(x_t)/L$ at even $t$, and at odd $t$ takes the extrapolated step $x_{t+1}=y_t-
abla f(y_t)/L$ with $y_t=x_t+ eta(x_t-x_{t-1})$). For even $t$, $f(x_{t+2})\le f(x_t)-\dfrac{1- eta^2}{2L}\|
abla f(x_t)\|^2-\dfrac1{2L}\|
abla f(y_{t+1})\|^2$, where $y_{t+1}=x_{t+1}+ eta(x_{t+1}-x_t)$. Consequently $\min_{t<2K,\ t\ \mathrm{even}}\|
abla f(x_t)\|^2\le\dfrac{2L igl(f(x_0)-f_{\inf} igr)}{(1- eta^2)K}$.
results.label: prop:ch5b:monotone

results.name: Exact joint spectral radius of the descent and injection matrices of Switching MM
results.summary: Because the descent matrix has rank one, the joint spectral radius of the descent and injection matrices of Switching MM is the larger of the spectral radius of the injection matrix and a supremum over a scalar sequence, a variant of a rank one device of Ahmadi and Parrilo (2012).
results.statement: For parameters $a$ and $\beta$ (in Switching MM on an eigendirection of a quadratic, $a=\alpha\lambda>0$ and $0\le\beta<1$), let $D=\begin{pmatrix}1-a&0\\1&0\end{pmatrix}$ and $N=\begin{pmatrix}(1-a)(1+\beta)&-(1-a)\beta\\1&0\end{pmatrix}$ be the matrices that map the state $(e_t,e_{t-1})$ to $(e_{t+1},e_t)$ for a descent step and for an injection step, and let $\hat\rho(\{D,N\})=\lim_{k\to\infty}\max_{M_i\in\{D,N\}}\|M_k\cdots M_1\|^{1/k}$ be their joint spectral radius. Write $D=vu^\top$ with $u=(1,0)^\top$ and $v=(1-a,1)^\top$, and put $\tau_j=u^\top N^jv$ for $j\ge0$. Then $\hat\rho(\{D,N\})=\max\Bigl(\rho(N),\ \sup_{j\ge0}|\tau_j|^{1/(j+1)}\Bigr)$, where $\rho(N)$ is the spectral radius of $N$.
results.label: prop:ch5b:jsr

results.name: Transient bound conjecture for the injection matrix of Switching MM
results.summary: Conjecture that the transient of repeated injection steps of Switching MM never exceeds the first descent factor, supported by computation on a grid of 200 momentum values and 300 normalized steps.
results.statement: Let $N=\begin{pmatrix}(1-a)(1+\beta)&-(1-a)\beta\\1&0\end{pmatrix}$, $u=(1,0)^\top$ and $v=(1-a,1)^\top$, and let $\tau_j=u^\top N^jv$ for $j\ge0$ (the first coordinate after $j$ injection steps of Switching MM, with normalized step $a$ and momentum coefficient $\beta$, started from the state left by one descent step). Conjecture: for all $a\in(0,1]$, $\beta\in[0,1)$ and $j\ge0$, $|\tau_j|\le1-a$.
results.label: conj:ch5b:transient

results.name: Every switching rule between descent and injection is stable on quadratics, conditional on the transient bound
results.status_text: conditional on the transient bound $|\tau_j|<1$ for every $j\ge0$ at the fixed normalized step $a$, where $\tau_j=u^\top N^jv$ is defined in the statement; it is the content of the transient bound conjecture ($|\tau_j|\le1-a$ for all $a\in(0,1]$, $\beta\in[0,1)$ and $j\ge0$), which has been checked numerically on a finite grid of parameters and is not proved
results.conditions: the transient bound $|\tau_j|<1$ for every $j\ge0$ at the fixed normalized step $a$, where $\tau_j=u^\top N^jv$ is defined in the statement; it is the content of the transient bound conjecture ($|\tau_j|\le1-a$ for all $a\in(0,1]$, $\beta\in[0,1)$ and $j\ge0$), which has been checked numerically on a finite grid of parameters and is not proved.
results.summary: If the transient bound holds, every switching rule between descent and injection steps of Switching MM, including adaptive and state dependent rules, is exponentially stable on a quadratic at step one over L.
results.statement: Let $0\le\beta<1$ and fix $a\in(0,1)$. On an eigendirection of a quadratic with eigenvalue $\lambda$ and normalized step $a=\alpha\lambda$, let $D(a)=\begin{pmatrix}1-a&0\\1&0\end{pmatrix}$ and $N(a)=\begin{pmatrix}(1-a)(1+\beta)&-(1-a)\beta\\1&0\end{pmatrix}$ be the matrices that map the state $(e_t,e_{t-1})$ to $(e_{t+1},e_t)$ for a descent step and for an injection step of Switching MM, let $\hat\rho(\{D(a),N(a)\})$ be their joint spectral radius, and let $\tau_j=u^\top N(a)^jv$ with $u=(1,0)^\top$ and $v=(1-a,1)^\top$. Suppose $|\tau_j|<1$ for all $j\ge0$. Then on a quadratic with spectrum in $(0,L]$ and step $\alpha=1/L$, every switching sequence between descent and injection steps, whether periodic, random, or chosen adaptively from the state, converges to the minimizer on the eigendirection with $a=\alpha\lambda$, with exponential rate at most $\hat\rho(\{D(a),N(a)\})<1$.
results.label: cor:ch5b:anyswitch

results.name: Exact linear rate of Switching MM on smooth strongly convex functions
results.summary: For strongly convex and L smooth functions, two steps of Switching MM at step one over L contract the distance to the minimizer by the product of the classical one step factors of a long and a short gradient step, which explicit functions show is the exact worst case over the class, and the function gap by its square, using the one step function value bound of Taylor, Hendrickx and Glineur (2018).
results.statement: Let $f$ be $\mu$ strongly convex and $L$ smooth with minimizer $x^\ast$, put $\kappa=L/\mu$, and run Switching MM with step $\alpha=1/L$ and momentum coefficient $\beta\in[0,1)$ (it starts from $x_{-1}=x_0$, takes the plain gradient step $x_{t+1}=x_t-\alpha\nabla f(x_t)$ at even $t$, and at odd $t$ takes the extrapolated step $x_{t+1}=y_t-\alpha\nabla f(y_t)$ with $y_t=x_t+\beta(x_t-x_{t-1})$). For every even $t$, $\|x_{t+2}-x^\ast\|\le q\,\|x_t-x^\ast\|$ with $q=q(\beta,\kappa)=\Bigl(1-\dfrac1\kappa\Bigr)\max\Bigl(1-\dfrac{1+\beta}{\kappa},\ \beta\Bigr)$, and $f(x_{t+2})-f^\ast\le q^2\,\bigl(f(x_t)-f^\ast\bigr)$.
results.label: thm:ch5b:rate

results.name: Speed of Switching MM relative to gradient descent on smooth strongly convex functions
results.summary: For condition numbers above an explicit threshold, the per step rate of Switching MM on the whole class of smooth strongly convex functions has normalized limit two plus beta over two, the slow mode step multiplier of the quadratic analysis, against one for gradient descent.
results.statement: Let $f$ be $\mu$ strongly convex and $L$ smooth with condition number $\kappa=L/\mu$, run Switching MM with step $1/L$ and momentum coefficient $\beta\in[0,1)$, and let $q=(1-1/\kappa)\max\bigl(1-(1+\beta)/\kappa,\ \beta\bigr)$ be the worst case, over this class of functions, of the factor by which two steps contract the distance to the minimizer. For $\kappa\ge(1+\beta)/(1-\beta)$ the per step rate of Switching MM is $q^{1/2}=\bigl((1-1/\kappa)(1-(1+\beta)/\kappa)\bigr)^{1/2}$, so that $-\kappa\log q^{1/2}\to(2+\beta)/2$ as $\kappa\to\infty$, against $1$ for gradient descent with the same step.
results.label: cor:ch5b:speed

results.name: Modified equation for period two gradient steps
results.summary: To second order, two gradient steps of lengths h1 and h2 follow the gradient flow of the objective plus a multiple of its squared gradient norm, with coefficient one quarter of the mean square step over the mean step; the single step case is the implicit gradient regularization of Barrett and Dherin (2021).
results.statement:
Let $f:\mathbb{R}^d	o\mathbb{R}$ be three times differentiable, write $G_h(x)=x-h
abla f(x)$, and consider the composition of gradient steps of lengths $h_1$ and $h_2$, in either order. To second order in $h=h_1+h_2$ (that is, up to terms of order $h^3$) it agrees with the time $h$ flow of the modified equation $\dot x=-
abla f(x)-\dfrac{h_1^2+h_2^2}{2(h_1+h_2)}\,
abla^2f(x)
abla f(x)=-
abla\Bigl(f+\dfrac{ ar h}{4}\|
abla f\|^2\Bigr)$, where $ ar h=\dfrac{h_1^2+h_2^2}{h_1+h_2}$.
results.label: prop:ch5b:modified

results.name: Convex rate for Switching MM when the long step is at most the golden ratio
results.summary: On smooth convex functions the bound for Switching MM after N steps is L R^2/((2+beta) N), against L R^2/(2N) for gradient descent by the same argument, provided the long step 1+beta is at most the golden ratio, as it is for the book's beta = log_2 3 minus 1.
results.statement: Let $f:\mathbb{R}^d\to\mathbb{R}$ be convex and differentiable with an $L$ Lipschitz gradient ($f$ is $L$ smooth), let $x_*$ be a minimizer of $f$ and $f_*=f(x_*)$, let $\varphi=(1+\sqrt5)/2$ be the golden ratio, and let $0\le\beta\le\varphi-1$. Let $x_0,x_1,x_2,\ldots$ be the iterates of Switching MM with step size $1/L$ and momentum $\beta$ started at $x_0$: put $x_{-1}=x_0$, and for $t\ge0$ let $x_{t+1}=x_t-\frac{1}{L}\nabla f(x_t)$ if $t$ is even, and $x_{t+1}=y_t-\frac{1}{L}\nabla f(y_t)$ with $y_t=x_t+\beta(x_t-x_{t-1})$ if $t$ is odd. Let $R=\|x_0-x_*\|$ (Euclidean norm). Then for every $j\ge0$, $(2+\beta)\bigl(f(x_{2j+2})-f_*\bigr)\le\frac{L}{2}\bigl(\|x_{2j}-x_*\|^2-\|x_{2j+2}-x_*\|^2\bigr)$, and consequently, for every even $N$, $f(x_N)-f_*\le\frac{LR^2}{(2+\beta)N}$.
results.label: thm:ch7b:smmrate

results.name: Exact convex worst case of Switching MM (conjecture)
results.summary: Conjectured exact worst case L R^2/((4+2 beta) N+2) of Switching MM on smooth convex functions for even N and beta up to about 0.686, supported by performance estimation computations and proved in a later chapter for N = 4, and for N = 2 when beta is at most 0.6446.
results.statement: Let $\beta_2=0.68614\ldots$ be the positive real root of $2\beta^3+5\beta^2-3=0$. Let $f:\mathbb{R}^d\to\mathbb{R}$ be convex and differentiable with an $L$ Lipschitz gradient ($f$ is $L$ smooth) and a minimizer $x_*$ (with $f_*=f(x_*)$), and let $x_0,x_1,x_2,\ldots$ be the iterates of Switching MM with step size $1/L$ and momentum $\beta$ started at $x_0$: put $x_{-1}=x_0$, and for $t\ge0$ let $x_{t+1}=x_t-\frac{1}{L}\nabla f(x_t)$ if $t$ is even, and $x_{t+1}=y_t-\frac{1}{L}\nabla f(y_t)$ with $y_t=x_t+\beta(x_t-x_{t-1})$ if $t$ is odd. Conjecture: for $0\le\beta\le\beta_2$ and every even $N$, the worst case of Switching MM over convex $L$ smooth functions with $\|x_0-x_*\|\le R$ (the supremum over all dimensions $d$, all such $f$ and all such $x_0$) is $\sup\bigl(f(x_N)-f_*\bigr)=\frac{LR^2}{(4+2\beta)N+2}$.
results.label: conj:ch7b:tight

results.name: Acceleration by similar triangles survives every switching rule
results.summary: Mixing similar triangles steps with plain gradient steps in any order, even one that depends on the iterates, never increases the energy, so the 1/J^2 rate in the number J of similar triangles steps is kept.
results.label: prop:ch7b:switch

results.name: Bregman decomposition of the logarithmic change along a Syracuse orbit
results.summary: Along any Syracuse orbit the change of the logarithm is exactly a linear term minus a sum of Itakura Saito divergences, and in the stochastic model the linear term is a martingale and the dissipation has mean log(4/3) per step, the size of the drift.
results.statement: Let $S(y)=(3y+1)/2^{v_2(3y+1)}$ be the Syracuse map on odd positive integers, where $v_2$ is the $2$ adic valuation, and let $D(t)=t-1-\log t\ge0$ for $t>0$ (the Itakura and Saito divergence of $t$ from $1$). For an odd positive integer $y_0$ let $y_{i+1}=S(y_i)$, $k_i=v_2(3y_i+1)$ and $M_i=y_{i+1}/y_i=(3+1/y_i)/2^{k_i}$. Then for every odd $y_0$ and every $N$, $\log y_N-\log y_0=\sum_{i<N}(M_i-1)-\sum_{i<N}D(M_i)$. In the stochastic model in which the $M_i$ are independent copies of $M=3/2^k$ with $k$ geometric, $\mathbb{P}(k=j)=2^{-j}$ for $j\ge1$, the partial sums $\sum_{i<N}(M_i-1)$ form a martingale in $N$, $\mathbb{E}M=1$, and the expected dissipation per step equals the drift exactly, $\mathbb{E}D(M)=-\mathbb{E}\log M=\log(4/3)$.
results.label: prop:ch7b:bregman

results.name: Uniform lower bound on the Bregman dissipation of the Syracuse map
results.summary: At every odd y at least 3 the Itakura Saito divergence of the Syracuse multiplier S(y)/y from 1 is at least 0.029092, with equality only at y = 9, and its limit inferior as y grows is 0.037682.
results.statement: Let $S(y)=(3y+1)/2^{v_2(3y+1)}$ be the Syracuse map on odd positive integers, where $v_2$ is the $2$ adic valuation, and let $D(t)=t-1-\log t$ for $t>0$. Then for every odd $y\ge3$, $D\bigl(S(y)/y\bigr)\ge c_*=D\bigl(\tfrac{7}{9}\bigr)=\log\tfrac{9}{7}-\tfrac{2}{9}=0.029092\ldots$, with equality only at $y=9$, and $\liminf_{y\to\infty}D\bigl(S(y)/y\bigr)=D\bigl(\tfrac{3}{4}\bigr)=\log\tfrac{4}{3}-\tfrac{1}{4}=0.037682\ldots$, where $y$ runs over odd integers.
results.label: prop:ch7b:dissipation

results.name: Diophantine insufficiency, infinitely many cycle lengths survive any verification range
results.summary: However far the verification of the Collatz conjecture is pushed, infinitely many cycle lengths survive the cycle inequality, so information about the approximation of log2 3 alone cannot exclude all nontrivial cycles, a point Halbeisen and Hungerbühler (1997) made earlier in another form.
results.statement: Let $\theta=\log_2 3$, let $\log$ denote the natural logarithm, and for an integer $r\geq1$ let $\delta(r)=\lceil r\theta\rceil-r\theta$ be the distance from $r\theta$ up to the next integer. Say that $r$ is excluded at verification range $X$ if $\delta(r)\geq r/(3X\log2)$. (If every element of every nontrivial cycle of the Syracuse map on the positive integers is at least $X$, then such a cycle with $r$ odd elements can exist only for an $r$ that is not excluded at $X$. The Syracuse map sends an odd $y$ to $(3y+1)/2^{v_2(3y+1)}$, where $v_2$ is the 2 adic valuation.) For every real $X\geq1$ there are infinitely many integers $r\geq1$ with $0<\delta(r)<\dfrac{r}{3X\log2}$, that is, infinitely many $r$ that are not excluded at verification range $X$.
results.label: prop:ch8:insufficient

results.name: Window lemma, the least element of a cycle lies in an explicit window
results.summary: Every element of a hypothetical Collatz cycle with m odd steps is at least an explicit lower bound and the least element is below the standard upper bound, so it lies in a window whose endpoints differ by a factor of about m over 3.
results.statement: Let $T$ be the accelerated Collatz map on the positive integers, $T(x)=x/2$ for even $x$ and $T(x)=(3x+1)/2$ for odd $x$. Let $x_1,\dots,x_r$ be the odd elements of a cycle of $T$ with $m=r$ odd steps and $k$ steps of $T$ in all (one turn of the cycle), and put $\Lambda=k\log2-m\log3>0$, where $\log$ is the natural logarithm. Then every element $x$ of the cycle, odd or even, satisfies $\frac{3^m-2^m}{2^k-3^m}\le x$, and $M=\min_i x_i$ satisfies $M<\frac{m}{3\Lambda}\le F(m)$, where $F(m)=\frac{m}{3\,\delta(m)\log2}$, $\delta(m)=\lceil m\theta\rceil-m\theta$ and $\theta=\log_2 3$. Here $\frac{3^m-2^m}{2^k-3^m}=\frac{1-(2/3)^m}{e^{\Lambda}-1}$, and $\frac{m}{3\Lambda}=F(m)$ exactly when $k=\lceil m\theta\rceil$. In particular the least element lies in the window $\Bigl[\frac{1-(2/3)^m}{e^{\Lambda}-1},\ \frac{m}{3\Lambda}\Bigr)$, whose endpoints have ratio $\frac m3\cdot\frac{e^{\Lambda}-1}{\Lambda}\bigl(1-(2/3)^m\bigr)^{-1}$, which is $\frac m3(1+o(1))$ as $\Lambda\to0$ and $m\to\infty$.
results.label: lem:ch8:window

results.name: What arithmetic would suffice to exclude all Collatz cycles
results.status_text: conditional on the hypothesis that, for the function $f$ of the statement, every nontrivial cycle of the accelerated map with $m$ odd steps and $k$ steps in all has least element $M<m/(3\Lambda f(m))$, where $\Lambda=k\log2-m\log3$; no such bound is proved in the book
results.conditions: the hypothesis that, for the function $f$ of the statement, every nontrivial cycle of the accelerated map with $m$ odd steps and $k$ steps in all has least element $M<m/(3\Lambda f(m))$, where $\Lambda=k\log2-m\log3$; no such bound is proved in the book.
results.summary: If an argument using the arithmetic of the parity word improved the standard upper bound on the least element of a cycle by a factor slightly above m over 3 for all large m, a finite verification would exclude every nontrivial cycle.
results.statement: Let $T$ be the accelerated Collatz map on the positive integers, $T(x)=x/2$ for even $x$ and $T(x)=(3x+1)/2$ for odd $x$, and call a cycle of $T$ nontrivial if it is not $\{1,2\}$. Let $\log$ be the natural logarithm, $\theta=\log_2 3$, $\delta(m)=\lceil m\theta\rceil-m\theta$ and $F(m)=\frac{m}{3\,\delta(m)\log2}$. For a cycle with $m$ odd steps and $k$ steps in all, let $M$ be its least element and $\Lambda=k\log2-m\log3$. Suppose that for some function $f$ every nontrivial cycle with $m$ odd steps and $k$ steps in all satisfied the sharpened upper bound $M<\frac{m}{3\Lambda f(m)}$. (i) If $f(m)\ge\frac m3\cdot\frac{e^{\Lambda}-1}{\Lambda}\bigl(1-(2/3)^m\bigr)^{-1}$ for every pair $(m,k)$ with $m\theta<k<2m$, then there are no nontrivial cycles. (ii) If $f(m)\ge\frac m3(1+\eta)$ for some $\eta>0$ and all $m\ge m_0$, where $(1+\eta)\bigl(1-(2/3)^{m_0}\bigr)>1$, let $\Lambda_0>0$ solve $\frac{e^{\Lambda_0}-1}{\Lambda_0}=(1+\eta)\bigl(1-(2/3)^{m_0}\bigr)$. Then every nontrivial cycle with $m\ge m_0$ odd steps has least element $M<C=\frac{1}{(1+\eta)\Lambda_0}$, which is about $\frac1{2\eta}$ when $\eta$ is small and $m_0$ is large. Consequently, if every element of every nontrivial cycle of positive integers is at least $X$ (a verified range, which holds for instance when every positive integer below $X$ reaches $1$) and $X\ge\max\bigl(C,\max_{m<m_0}F(m)\bigr)$, then there are no nontrivial cycles.
results.label: cor:ch8:window

results.name: Cesàro identity for the halving exponents of a Syracuse orbit
results.summary: Over N strides of the Syracuse map, the logarithmic change of the orbit equals a sum of logarithms minus N times the running mean of the halving exponents times log 2, which ties growth of the orbit to that running mean.
results.statement: Let $S$ be the Syracuse map, which sends an odd positive integer $y$ to $(3y+1)/2^{v_2(3y+1)}$, where $v_2$ is the 2 adic valuation. For an odd positive integer $x_0$ let $y_j=S^{(j)}(x_0)$ be the iterates ($y_0=x_0$), let $k_j=v_2(3y_{j-1}+1)\geq1$ be the halving exponents, so that $y_j=(3y_{j-1}+1)/2^{k_j}$, and let $\bar k_N=\frac1N\sum_{j=1}^Nk_j$. Let $\log$ be the natural logarithm. Then for every odd positive integer $x_0$ and every $N\geq1$, $\log y_N-\log x_0=\sum_{j=1}^{N}\log\Bigl(3+\frac{1}{y_{j-1}}\Bigr)-N\bar k_N\log2$. Equivalently, $\bar k_N=\log_2 3+\frac{1}{N}\Bigl(\log_2x_0-\log_2y_N+\sum_{j=1}^{N}\log_2\Bigl(1+\frac{1}{3y_{j-1}}\Bigr)\Bigr)$. Consequently, if the orbit of $x_0>1$ reaches $1$ at stride $N$ (that is, $y_N=1$), then $\bar k_N>\log_2 3+\frac{\log_2x_0}{N}>\log_2 3$.
results.label: prop:cesaro

results.name: Cesàro liminf conjecture on the running mean of the halving exponents
results.summary: Along every Syracuse orbit the lower limit of the running average of the halving exponents is strictly above log2 3, a statement the book shows is equivalent to the divergence half of the Collatz conjecture.
results.statement: Let $S$ be the Syracuse map, which sends an odd positive integer $y$ to $(3y+1)/2^{v_2(3y+1)}$, where $v_2$ is the 2 adic valuation. For an odd positive integer $x_0$ let $y_j=S^{(j)}(x_0)$ be the iterates ($y_0=x_0$) and $k_j=v_2(3y_{j-1}+1)$ the halving exponents. Conjecture: for every odd positive integer $x_0$, $\liminf_{N\to\infty}\frac1N\sum_{j=1}^Nk_j>\log_2 3$.
results.label: conj:cesaro

results.name: A bounded form of Tao's theorem would imply the Collatz conjecture, given the positive density theorems
results.status_text: conditional on the positive density theorem of Mazur (2026) or of Lau (2026), recent unrefereed preprints with Lean formalizations whose proofs the book does not check: for every integer $t\ge1$ not divisible by $3$, the set of positive integers whose orbit under the Collatz map reaches $t$ has positive lower natural density; the computer verification of Bařina (2025) that every positive integer up to $2^{71}$ has an orbit that reaches $1$, which the book cites and does not repeat
results.conditions: the positive density theorem of Mazur (2026) or of Lau (2026), recent unrefereed preprints with Lean formalizations whose proofs the book does not check: for every integer $t\ge1$ not divisible by $3$, the set of positive integers whose orbit under the Collatz map reaches $t$ has positive lower natural density; the computer verification of Bařina (2025) that every positive integer up to $2^{71}$ has an orbit that reaches $1$, which the book cites and does not repeat
results.summary: If the positive density theorems of Mazur and Lau are right, the Collatz conjecture would follow from a bounded form of Tao's theorem, namely that the least value on the orbit of n is at most 2 to the power 71 for all n in a set of logarithmic density one.
results.statement: Let $T_0$ be the Collatz map on the positive integers, $T_0(n)=n/2$ for even $n$ and $T_0(n)=3n+1$ for odd $n$. The orbit of $n$ reaches $1$ if $T_0^{(k)}(n)=1$ for some $k\ge0$, and $\mathrm{Col}_{\min}(n)=\min_{k\ge0}T_0^{(k)}(n)$ is the least value on the orbit of $n$. For a set $A$ of positive integers, the lower and upper natural densities are the $\liminf$ and $\limsup$ as $x\to\infty$ of $x^{-1}\#\{n\le x:n\in A\}$, the lower and upper logarithmic densities are the $\liminf$ and $\limsup$ of $(\log x)^{-1}\sum_{n\le x,\,n\in A}1/n$, and $A$ has logarithmic density one if both of the latter equal $1$. Assume the positive density theorem of Mazur or of Lau: for every integer $t\ge1$ not divisible by $3$, the set of positive integers whose orbit under $T_0$ reaches $t$ has positive lower natural density. Then (a) if the set of $n$ whose orbit reaches $1$ has logarithmic density one, every orbit reaches $1$: the positive density theorem gives this when the set has upper natural density one (the corollary of Mazur and of Lau), and for every set the lower natural density is at most the lower logarithmic density, which is at most the upper logarithmic density, which is at most the upper natural density, so logarithmic density one implies upper natural density one. And (b) since every positive integer up to $2^{71}$ reaches $1$ (verified by Bařina), if $\mathrm{Col}_{\min}(n)\le2^{71}$ for all $n$ in a set of logarithmic density one, then the set of $n$ whose orbit reaches $1$ has logarithmic density one, so every orbit reaches $1$ and the Collatz conjecture holds. Tao's theorem proves the hypothesis of (b) with $2^{71}$ replaced by any function $f(n)$ that tends to infinity.
results.label: prop:ch9b:bounded

results.name: Residue certificates cannot prove descent for all integers (the exceptional 2 adic set)
results.summary: No residue certificate of finite level can certify descent for every integer, because every residue class it leaves uncovered contains infinitely many positive integers, while the 2 adic integers with infinite coefficient stopping time form a closed null set that contains a point of each known negative cycle.
results.statement: Let $T$ be the accelerated Collatz map on the $2$ adic integers $\mathbb{Z}_2$, given by $T(x)=x/2$ for even $x$ and $T(x)=(3x+1)/2$ for odd $x$, and for $x\in\mathbb{Z}_2$ and $j\ge1$ let $m_j(x)$ be the number of odd values among $x,T(x),\ldots,T^{(j-1)}(x)$. A residue class modulo $2^k$ is uncovered at level $k$ if its members have $3^{m_j}>2^j$ for every $1\le j\le k$, that is, if their coefficient stopping time $\tau=\min\{j\ge1:3^{m_j}<2^j\}$ exceeds $k$; a residue certificate of level $k$ covers exactly the other classes (every sufficiently large member of such a class falls below itself within $k$ steps). Let $E_k\subset\mathbb{Z}_2$ be the union of the classes uncovered at level $k$, and let $E=\{x\in\mathbb{Z}_2:3^{m_j(x)}>2^j\text{ for every }j\ge1\}$ be the set of $2$ adic integers with infinite coefficient stopping time. Then: (i) $E$ is a closed subset of $\mathbb{Z}_2$ of Haar measure zero, $E=\bigcap_{k\ge1}E_k$, and $E$ contains $-1$, $-5$ and $-17$, one point of each of the three known cycles of $T$ on the negative integers. (ii) Every uncovered class at every level contains infinitely many positive integers. Hence no residue certificate of finite level covers all integers $n\ge2$. (iii) If a positive integer $n\ge2$ lies in $E$, its orbit under $T$ never falls below $n$. Hence if every integer $n\ge2$ has a finite stopping time (the descent form of the Collatz conjecture, where the stopping time of $n$ is $\min\{k\ge1:T^{(k)}(n)<n\}$), then no integer $n\ge2$ lies in $E$; conversely, if no integer $n\ge2$ lies in $E$ and the coefficient stopping time conjecture of Terras holds (the stopping time of every $n\ge2$ equals its coefficient stopping time), then every $n\ge2$ has a finite stopping time.
results.label: prop:ch10b:residue

results.name: Two energies under Haar measure, the coefficient stopping time and the total stopping time
results.summary: The level sets of the coefficient stopping time are unions of residue classes with exactly computable volume, while the total stopping time is almost surely infinite under Haar measure, which separates what a sampler can reach from what the conjecture is about.
results.statement: Let $\mu$ be the Haar probability measure on the $2$ adic integers $\mathbb{Z}_2$ and $T$ the accelerated Collatz map, $T(x)=x/2$ for even $x$ and $T(x)=(3x+1)/2$ for odd $x$. For $x\in\mathbb{Z}_2$ let $m_k(x)$ be the number of odd values among $x,T(x),\ldots,T^{(k-1)}(x)$, let $\tau(x)=\min\{k\ge1:3^{m_k(x)}<2^k\}$ be the coefficient stopping time, and let $\sigma_\infty(x)=\min\{k\ge0:T^{(k)}(x)=1\}$ be the total stopping time counted in steps of $T$ (both equal $\infty$ if the set is empty). Let $F(m)=\mu\{\tau\le m\}$, call a binary word alive if every prefix of length $i\ge1$ with $l$ ones satisfies $3^l>2^i$, and let $N_m(j)$ be the number of alive words of length $m$ with $j$ ones. Then: (i) For every $m$ the level set $\{\tau>m\}\subset\mathbb{Z}_2$ is a union of residue classes modulo $2^m$, hence open and closed, and its Haar measure is $Z_\tau(m)=1-F(m)=2^{-m}\sum_jN_m(j)$, which is computable exactly in $O(m^2)$ arithmetic operations by the recursion $N_k(j)=[3^j>2^k]\,(N_{k-1}(j)+N_{k-1}(j-1))$ with $N_0(0)=1$ and $N_{k-1}(-1)=0$. The sets $\{\tau>m\}$ decrease in $m$ and their intersection $\{\tau=\infty\}$ has measure zero. (ii) For every $m$ the set $\{x\in\mathbb{Z}_2:\sigma_\infty(x)\le m\}$ is finite, and it contains at most one positive integer in each residue class modulo $2^m$. Consequently $\{\sigma_\infty>m\}$ has Haar measure one for every $m$, and so does the intersection $\{\sigma_\infty=\infty\}$ of these sets: the energy $\sigma_\infty$ is almost surely infinite under $\mu$, and any simulation with this energy must use a uniform prior on a finite range, which the book takes to be the integers in $[2,2^B)$, with $Z_\sigma(m)=\#\{2\le n<2^B:\sigma_\infty(n)>m\}/(2^B-2)$.
results.label: prop:ch10b:horizons

results.name: Perfect split sampling for the coefficient stopping time
results.summary: An exact sampler with no inner Markov chain draws residues whose coefficient stopping time exceeds a given depth, in time linear in the depth after a quadratic table, even when their prior mass is exponentially small.
results.statement: Let $\mu$ be the Haar probability measure on $\mathbb{Z}_2$, let $T$ be the accelerated Collatz map ($T(x)=x/2$ for even $x$ and $(3x+1)/2$ for odd $x$), let $m_k(x)$ be the number of odd values among $x,T(x),\ldots,T^{(k-1)}(x)$, and let $\tau(x)=\min\{k\ge1:3^{m_k(x)}<2^k\}$ be the coefficient stopping time ($\tau=\infty$ if there is no such $k$), a function of the residue class of $x$. Put $Z_0=1$ and $Z_k=\mu\{\tau>k\}$, and let $R_k$ be the number of residue classes modulo $2^k$ with $\tau=k$ (so $R_k>0$ exactly when $Z_k<Z_{k-1}$). Fix a depth $K\ge1$, let the levels be the integers $0\le k\le K$, put $\tau_K=\min(\tau,K+1)$, and let the discrete weights be $\omega_0=1$ and $\omega_k=1/Z_k-1/Z_{k-1}$ for $1\le k\le K$, so that $W(l)=\sum_{k<l}\omega_k=1/Z_{l-1}$ for $1\le l\le K+1$. Then the augmented law $\pi_\omega(x,k)\propto[\tau_K(x)>k]\,\mu(dx)\,\omega_k$ on $\mathbb{Z}_2\times\{0,\ldots,K\}$ has the finite mass $1+\sum_{k=1}^K\lambda_k$, where $\lambda_k=Z_k\omega_k=1-Z_k/Z_{k-1}$ is the hazard, and its Gibbs sampler can be run exactly, with no Markov chain inside the level sets: (i) given $x$, the level $k$ is drawn from the weights $\omega_k$ restricted to $\{0,\ldots,\tau_K(x)-1\}$, a finite discrete law; (ii) given $k$, a point with law $\mu$ restricted to $\{\tau>k\}$ is drawn exactly, as far as $\tau_K$ can see it, which is to say its residue modulo $2^K$. For this, call a binary word alive if every prefix of length $i\ge1$ with $l$ ones satisfies $3^l>2^i$, and let $N_i(j)$ be the number of alive words of length $i$ with $j$ ones. An alive word of length $k$ is drawn uniformly by backward sampling: the terminal count $j$ is chosen with probability $N_k(j)/\sum_{j'}N_k(j')$, and the parities are generated from the last to the first, with probability $N_{i-1}(j)/N_i(j)$ of a zero and $N_{i-1}(j-1)/N_i(j)$ of a one (reducing $j$ by one after a one). The word is followed by $K-k$ independent fair parities, and the word of length $K$ is converted to a residue modulo $2^K$ by the Terras bijection between residues modulo $2^K$ and parity words of length $K$. The cost is $O(K)$ per draw after an $O(K^2)$ table. The level marginal of the chain is proportional to $1$ at $k=0$ and to $\lambda_k$ for $1\le k\le K$, and the $x$ marginal is proportional to $\mu$ weighted by $1/Z_{\tau_K(x)-1}$, so that the event $\{\tau>K\}$ has stationary probability $1/(1+\sum_{k\le K}\lambda_k)$. Every level $k\le K$ with $R_k>0$ is visited with the positive frequency $\lambda_k/(1+\sum_{k'\le K}\lambda_{k'})$. Without the truncation the augmented law has infinite mass, since $\prod_{k\le K}(1-\lambda_k)=Z_K\to0$ forces $\sum_k\lambda_k=\infty$, and every level is then visited with long run frequency zero.
results.label: thm:ch10b:perfect

results.name: Coalescence of orbits shifts the total stopping time
results.summary: If the orbits of two positive integers meet at a point other than 1 or 2, their total stopping times differ by exactly the difference of the numbers of steps each takes to reach it.
results.statement: Let $T$ be the accelerated Collatz map ($T(n)=n/2$ for even $n$ and $T(n)=(3n+1)/2$ for odd $n$) and let $\sigma_\infty(n)=\min\{k\ge0:T^{(k)}(n)=1\}$ be the total stopping time of a positive integer $n$ in steps of $T$ ($\infty$ if there is no such $k$). Let $n$ and $n'$ be positive integers whose orbits meet at a point $x\ge3$, reached from $n$ after $s$ steps and from $n'$ after $s'$ steps. Then $\sigma_\infty(n')=\sigma_\infty(n)-s+s'$. In particular, if $s=s'$ (as when the two orbits occupy the pair $8k+4$, $8k+5$ with $k\ge1$ at the same step, and then coincide three steps later), then $n'$ lies in every level set $\{\sigma_\infty>m\}$ that contains $n$.
results.label: prop:ch10b:acceptance

results.name: Additive deficits of the second and third cumulants of total stopping times, fitted to the exact census
results.summary: A fit to the exact census of total stopping times shows that their second and third cumulants grow at the rate of the Bernoulli model up to constant additive deficits, which accounts for the observed skewness; it is a computation on the blocks from 2^20 to 2^30, not a proof for all starting values.
results.statement: Let $T$ be the accelerated Collatz map, $T(m)=m/2$ for even $m$ and $T(m)=(3m+1)/2$ for odd $m$, and let $\sigma_\infty(n)$ be the total stopping time of $n$, the number of steps of $T$ from $n$ to $1$ (the census computes it for every $n<2^{30}$). For each $k$ with $20\le k\le29$ let $n$ be uniform in the dyadic block $[2^k,2^{k+1})$, let $\kappa_2(\sigma_\infty)$ and $\kappa_3(\sigma_\infty)$ be the exact second and third cumulants of $\sigma_\infty(n)$, and let $\mathbb{E}\log n$ be the mean of $\log n$ over the block. Fitting $\kappa_2(\sigma_\infty)=a_2\,\mathbb{E}\log n-D_2$ and $\kappa_3(\sigma_\infty)=a_3\,\mathbb{E}\log n-D_3$ over these ten blocks gives slopes $a_2=101.06$ and $a_3=4430.2$, within $0.32$ and $0.13$ percent of the model values $A_2=\sigma^2/|\mu|^3=101.39$ and $A_3=3\sigma^4/|\mu|^5=4435.7$ of the Bernoulli model (drift $\mu=\log(\sqrt3/2)$ and step variance $\sigma^2=(\tfrac12\log3)^2$), and constant deficits $D_2=133.3$ and $D_3=34\,060$, in units of squared and cubed steps. The largest residuals of the fits over the ten blocks are $1.1$ and $89$.
results.label: prop:ch16:deficit

results.name: Conjectured exact worst case rate of Switching MM on smooth convex functions, both branches
results.summary: A conjectured closed form for the exact worst case of Switching MM on smooth convex functions, for every even number of steps and every momentum coefficient below one, with a main branch and an overshoot branch that cross at an explicit threshold.
results.statement: Let $0\le\beta<1$, let $N\ge2$ be even, and run Switching MM with step $1/L$ and momentum coefficient $\beta$ from $x_0$ (from each even iterate $x_{2j}$ it takes a gradient step of length $(1+\beta)/L$ to a point $y$, then a gradient step of length $1/L$ from $y$ to $x_{2j+2}$). Put $D_N=(4+2\beta)N+2$ and $D'_N=4N-2+2(N-2)\beta$. Conjecture: over all convex $L$ smooth functions $f$ with a minimizer $x_*$, $f_*=f(x_*)$, and $\|x_0-x_*\|\le R$, the worst case is $\sup\bigl(f(x_N)-f_*\bigr)=LR^2\max\bigl\{1/D_N,\ \beta^2/D'_N\bigr\}$. The two branches cross at $\beta_N=\bigl(\sqrt{9N^2-2N+1}-N-1\bigr)/(2N)$, the positive root of $N\beta^2+(N+1)\beta-(2N-1)=0$, so that the main branch $LR^2/D_N$ is exact for all even $N$ exactly when $\beta\le\beta_2=(\sqrt{33}-3)/4=0.68614$.
results.label: conj:ch16:full

results.name: Explicit worst case functions for Switching MM on smooth convex functions
results.summary: Two explicit one dimensional functions, a Huber function and an overshoot function, show that the worst case of Switching MM on smooth convex functions is at least the larger of the two branches of the conjectured exact rate, for every even number of steps and every momentum coefficient below one.
results.statement: Let $0\le\beta<1$, let $N\ge2$ be even, and run Switching MM with step $1/L$ and momentum coefficient $\beta$ from $x_0$ (from each even iterate $x_{2j}$ it takes a gradient step of length $(1+\beta)/L$ to a point $y$, then a gradient step of length $1/L$ from $y$ to $x_{2j+2}$). Put $D_N=(4+2\beta)N+2$ and $D'_N=4N-2+2(N-2)\beta$. Then the supremum of $f(x_N)-f_*$ over all convex $L$ smooth functions $f$ with a minimizer $x_*$, $f_*=f(x_*)$, and $\|x_0-x_*\|\le R$ satisfies $\sup\bigl(f(x_N)-f_*\bigr)\ge LR^2\max\bigl\{1/D_N,\ \beta^2/D'_N\bigr\}$.
results.label: prop:ch16:lower

results.name: Exact worst case rate of Switching MM after two and four steps, by an explicit certificate
results.summary: For two and four steps and momentum coefficients up to about 0.64 and 0.70, an explicit certificate built from interpolation inequalities proves the conjectured exact rate of Switching MM on smooth convex functions, in ranges that contain the Collatz momentum.

The form $q$ is nonnegative identically when $N=2$ and $0\le eta\le b_2=0.64461$, or $N=4$ and $0\le eta\le b_4=0.70438$, where $b_2$ and $b_4$ are the positive roots of $2 eta^4+11 eta^3+17 eta^2+ eta-11$ and $4 eta^4+21 eta^3+31 eta^2- eta-23$.
